source_meta._title: Soul Speed in minecart uses durability

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.1, unmodified vanilla client, single-player integrated server, Overworld, keyboard and mouse. Use Creative mode with cheats enabled to construct the deterministic rail setup, then change to Survival mode before placing and riding the minecart.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.1, the first version listed as affected. Do not use fix version 24w18a.
Use a new or disposable single-player world with commands/cheats available.
Do not use mods, plugins, datapacks, or altered game rules that change minecart movement, enchantments, item durability, or player equipment.
Have a clear, approximately 11-by-11-block flat area available in the Overworld.
Use newly generated leather boots containing only Soul Speed III; do not add Unbreaking or Mending.
The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, or dimension, so no particular seed or location is required.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for Java Edition 1.16.1, launch it, and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left version text on the main menu identifies the running game as Minecraft 1.16.1.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new world in Creative mode, and ensure commands/cheats are enabled. Enter the world and wait until surrounding terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded single-player world, can fly, and has access to the Creative inventory and commands.

steps.action: Locate a level area with room for a 9-by-9-block rail loop plus at least one clear block around every side. Remove vegetation or other blocks that would obstruct the track or its power sources.
steps.success_cue: An unobstructed area of at least 11 by 11 blocks is available.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Obtain Soul Soil, Rail, Powered Rail, Redstone Torch, and Minecart, and place them in accessible hotbar slots. The hotbar is the nine-slot row at the bottom of the screen; select its slots with the number keys 1 through 9 or the mouse wheel. Close the inventory with E.
steps.exact_input: Creative inventory search terms: Soul Soil; Rail; Powered Rail; Redstone Torch; Minecart
steps.success_cue: Soul Soil, ordinary rails, powered rails, redstone torches, and a minecart are available in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: At ground level, replace or cover the perimeter of a 9-by-9-block square with Soul Soil. Use Soul Soil on all four sides, including the four corners, while leaving the 7-by-7 interior empty or unchanged. The perimeter contains 32 Soul Soil blocks.
steps.success_cue: A closed square ring of Soul Soil surrounds a 7-by-7-block interior, with no gaps in the ring.

steps.action: Build a closed rail loop directly on top of the Soul Soil ring. Place one ordinary Rail on each of the four corner blocks so that each corner becomes a curved rail. On each side, fill all seven positions between the corner rails with Powered Rails.
steps.exact_input: 4 ordinary corner Rails and 28 Powered Rails
steps.success_cue: The rails form one continuous closed loop, every rail is supported directly by Soul Soil, and all four ordinary corner rails visibly connect the two adjoining straight sides.

steps.action: Power the straight sections. At the midpoint outside each of the four sides, place a Redstone Torch on top of the adjacent ground block beside a Powered Rail. Inspect the rails; powered rails should appear bright red. If any powered rail remains dark, place an additional Redstone Torch on an adjacent solid block until that rail and the connected straight section are powered.
steps.success_cue: Every Powered Rail in the loop is visibly lit, while the four ordinary corner rails still form an unbroken loop.

steps.action: Enable advanced item tooltips for the later durability inspection. Press F3+H together and read the status message. If the message says that advanced tooltips are hidden, press F3+H once more so the final message says they are shown. On keyboards that reserve function keys, hold Fn as required.
steps.success_cue: A status message reports "Advanced tooltips: shown" or the equivalent localized message.

steps.action: Change to Survival mode. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds, hearts and hunger icons are visible, and the player is in Survival mode.

steps.action: Press E to open the Survival inventory and inspect the foot armor slot, located at the bottom of the vertical armor-slot column beside the player model. If any boots are present, move them into an ordinary inventory slot. Press E to close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: The player's foot armor slot is empty before the test boots are supplied.

steps.action: Select the Minecart in the hotbar. Aim at a Powered Rail on a straight section of the loop and right-click once to place the minecart.
steps.success_cue: One empty minecart is resting on a powered straight section of the rail loop.

steps.action: With an empty hand or any non-placeable selected item, aim at the minecart and right-click it to mount it. Do not press the dismount control, which is Left Shift by default.
steps.success_cue: The viewpoint is seated inside the minecart and the player is a passenger of that minecart.

steps.action: While mounted, hold W briefly to nudge the minecart along the powered rail. Release W once the powered rails have accelerated it.
steps.success_cue: The occupied minecart is moving around the loop without the player dismounting.

steps.action: Allow the minecart to complete at least one full circuit before equipping the boots. Confirm that it passes all four corners and continues moving without stopping. If it stops, remain mounted, use W to restart it, and correct any unpowered or disconnected rail before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The occupied minecart has completed a full loop and continues circulating over rails supported by Soul Soil.

steps.action: While still mounted in the moving minecart, press T to open in-game chat. Do not press Left Shift or otherwise dismount.
steps.success_cue: The chat input is open while the player remains a passenger in the minecart.

steps.action: Enter the following 1.16.1-compatible command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This equips a new pair of leather boots enchanted only with Soul Speed III in the player's foot armor slot.
steps.success_cue: The command reports successful replacement of the armor slot; the player remains mounted, and new Soul Speed III leather boots occupy the foot armor slot.

steps.action: After executing the equipment command, leave the boots equipped and remain in the minecart while it continues circulating over the Soul-Soil-supported rail loop for approximately 30 seconds. Do not dismount. Count only time during which the minecart is moving; if it stops, restart it with W while remaining mounted and continue until approximately 30 seconds of mounted movement has elapsed.
steps.exact_input: Approximately 30 seconds; do not press Left Shift
steps.success_cue: Approximately 30 seconds of mounted minecart travel have elapsed since the Soul Speed III boots were equipped, and the player is still wearing the boots and riding on the Soul-Soil-supported loop.

stor.handoff_condition: Approximately 30 seconds of continuous mounted travel have just elapsed with the Soul Speed III leather boots equipped. The player remains in Survival mode, mounted in the moving minecart, and traveling on rails placed directly over Soul Soil. Hand control to the observation subsystem for item-durability inspection.
uncertainties: The contents of setup.png and the example video were not supplied in the raw report. The 9-by-9 powered loop is therefore a deterministic reconstruction of the text requirement that the player ride a minecart track placed on Soul Soil; it may not duplicate the attachment's exact dimensions or power layout.

The equipment command shown in the 21w40a comment uses `/item replace`, but recommended version 1.16.1 predates that command. This plan explicitly adapts it to `/replaceitem`; Minecraft Wiki documents that `/replaceitem` was replaced by `/item` in 20w46a/1.17. ([de.minecraft.wiki](https://de.minecraft.wiki/w/Befehl/replaceitem?utm_source=openai))

The report specifies only "around thirty seconds," not an exact exposure duration. This plan uses approximately 30 seconds of actual minecart movement and does not require repeated or extended triggering.
No world seed, coordinates, or dimension are specified. An Overworld location and a newly constructed powered loop are practical execution choices rather than report-mandated conditions.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-275203:Minecarts always spawn facing east/west and move upward slightly when being placed on rails | Duplicate:inward:MC-275356:VERY strange visual minecart behavior (Look at Picture and Video!)
source_meta._title: Minecart not oriented correctly when placed on a sloped unpowered powered rail

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w33a in a single-player Creative-mode world with the Minecart Improvements experiment enabled. No particular seed, coordinates, or dedicated server is specified by the report.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher is able to install and start Java Edition snapshot 24w33a.
Create a new world for this reproduction because the Minecart Improvements experiment must be enabled from the Experiments screen during world creation.
Use the Minecart Improvements experiment; the report comment states that the issue only occurs with this experimental toggle enabled.
Use Item/Place Block must be bound to an available control; its default input is right-click.
Use an open build area without adjacent redstone power sources so that the powered rail remains unpowered.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select a Java Edition installation that uses snapshot 24w33a, and start the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition main menu is open and displays version 24w33a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is visible.

steps.action: Set the new world's game mode to Creative so the required building materials can be acquired without unrelated crafting or exploration.
steps.success_cue: The world creation screen shows Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Open the experiment settings and enable the experiment named Minecart Improvements. Do not substitute the Redstone Experiments toggle or leave Minecart Improvements disabled.
steps.success_cue: The Minecart Improvements control is visibly set to ON.

steps.action: Return from the Experiments screen and create the world. If an experimental-world warning appears, accept it and continue.
steps.exact_input: Done -> Create New World; confirm Proceed if prompted
steps.success_cue: The player has entered the newly created world.

steps.action: Wait before building until nearby terrain has rendered and normal movement and camera controls respond without world-loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: Nearby blocks are rendered, the player can move normally, and the world is ready for block placement.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory, select the Search Items tab, search for Stone, and move Stone into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine immediately selectable slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: Stone is present in a hotbar slot.

steps.action: In the Creative inventory search, find Powered Rail and move it into a different hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: Powered Rail is present in a hotbar slot.

steps.action: In the Creative inventory search, find the ordinary Minecart item and move it into a different hotbar slot. Use the item named Minecart, not Minecart with Chest, Minecart with Hopper, Minecart with TNT, or Minecart with Furnace.
steps.success_cue: An ordinary Minecart item is present in a hotbar slot.

steps.action: Close the inventory and move to a clear, approximately 3-by-3-block area that has no redstone torches, redstone blocks, powered redstone dust, levers, buttons, or other potential rail power sources next to the intended build.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed and an unobstructed, unpowered build area is available.

steps.action: Select Stone in the hotbar and place one Stone block on the ground. Designate this single block as the lower support.
steps.exact_input: Select the Stone hotbar slot; right-click the ground once
steps.success_cue: One Stone block is present as the lower support.

steps.action: Place a second Stone block directly adjacent to the lower support, then place one more Stone block on top of that second block. This produces two adjacent support columns: one column one block tall and the other two blocks tall.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the adjacent ground position; right-click the top face of the newly placed block
steps.success_cue: A one-block-tall Stone support and a directly adjacent two-block-tall Stone support are present.

steps.action: Select Powered Rail and place one on the top face of the one-block-tall support.
steps.exact_input: Select the Powered Rail hotbar slot; right-click the top of the one-block-tall support
steps.success_cue: A Powered Rail is resting on the lower support.

steps.action: Place another Powered Rail on the top face of the adjacent two-block-tall support so the two rails connect across the one-block height difference.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the top of the two-block-tall support
steps.success_cue: The rail on the lower support has changed into a diagonal segment that rises toward the rail on the taller support.

steps.action: Confirm that the diagonal target rail is a Powered Rail and is not receiving redstone power. If desired, aim at it and use the F3 debug screen to check that the targeted block is minecraft:powered_rail with an ascending shape and powered set to false, then close the debug screen before continuing.
steps.exact_input: F3; verify Targeted Block properties; F3
steps.success_cue: The target is a visibly sloped Powered Rail, no redstone source is powering it, and the normal game view is restored.

steps.action: Select the ordinary Minecart item in the hotbar. Do not mount or dispense it.
steps.exact_input: Press the number key corresponding to the Minecart hotbar slot, or scroll to that slot
steps.success_cue: Minecart is the active hotbar item and is visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair directly at the diagonal surface of the lower, sloped, unpowered Powered Rail. Ensure the crosshair is not aimed at the flat rail on the upper support or at either Stone support block.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is centered on the diagonal Powered Rail that rises between the two support heights.

steps.action: Use the Minecart item once on the sloped, unpowered Powered Rail, using the default right-click control. Do not push, enter, strike, or otherwise interact with the resulting minecart after placement.
steps.success_cue: A minecart entity has just been created on the diagonal Powered Rail, with no subsequent interaction performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The ordinary minecart has just been placed directly onto the sloped, unpowered Powered Rail in the 24w33a world with Minecart Improvements enabled. Stop player input and begin observing the newly placed minecart's orientation.
uncertainties: The report's exact build diagram was contained in image attachments that were not included in the supplied report text and were not publicly readable from the issue page. The plan therefore reconstructs the minimum supported setup: a Powered Rail sloping upward by one block and receiving no redstone power.

The original attachment may have used different support blocks, cardinal orientation, surrounding rails, or a longer slope. None of those details are available in the supplied text, so Stone supports and a two-rail one-block incline are practical implementation choices rather than asserted report requirements.

The report does not specify a seed, coordinates, game mode, or multiplayer/server requirement. A new single-player Creative world is selected solely to remove item-acquisition randomness while retaining the required experimental toggle.

The comment describes dispenser placement as an additional reproduction variant requiring a one-tick pulse, but the primary report already supplies the simpler player-placement trigger. The dispenser variant is intentionally omitted from the main execution path.

source_meta._title: Derailed minecarts snap onto nearby rails after falling down

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w33a in a newly created single-player world with the Minecart Improvements experiment enabled. Creative mode is recommended as a practical execution choice so the setup can be built and its two upper components can be broken accurately without tool or mining-delay requirements.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 24w33a, not the fixed snapshot 24w34a.
Create a new world for this test; Minecart Improvements is an experimental feature that must be enabled during world creation in 24w33a.

At world creation, navigate through More -> Experiments, set Minecart Improvements to ON, confirm the experimental-world warning if shown, and then create the world. This activation method is confirmed by the official 24w33a snapshot notes. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/es-es/article/minecraft-snapshot-24w33a?utm_source=openai))
Use Creative mode as a practical choice. No seed, coordinates, world type, server requirement, commands, or game rule changes are specified by the report.
Have one minecart, one powered rail, one normal rail, and several solid full blocks available in the inventory.
Use an open area where the vertically stacked test structure and the falling minecart will remain visible.

The report refers to an attached setup image whose block-by-block contents are not present in the supplied report text. The steps below use the minimum deterministic vertical arrangement supported by the written actions: a minecart on an upper powered rail and removable support block, with a normal rail directly below the fall path.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using the 24w33a installation/profile and wait for the title screen to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left corner of the title screen identifies the running version as 24w33a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world creation screen and select Creative mode. Creative mode is not stated by the report, but it provides the required blocks and allows the powered rail and support block to be removed immediately and accurately.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen shows Creative as the selected game mode.

steps.action: Open the experimental-feature menu, enable Minecart Improvements, return to the world creation screen, and accept any warning that the world uses experimental features.
steps.exact_input: More -> Experiments -> Minecart Improvements: ON -> Done
steps.success_cue: Minecart Improvements remains enabled and the world creation screen is ready to continue.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until terrain is rendered and normal player movement responds without loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the new world, nearby terrain is visible, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the inventory action, whose default key is E. Obtain a Minecart, Powered Rail, Rail, and at least six solid full blocks. Place these items into accessible hotbar slots, then close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.exact_input: E; select Minecart, Powered Rail, Rail, and solid full blocks
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a minecart, a powered rail, a normal rail, and solid full blocks.

steps.action: Move to an open, level location. If necessary in Creative mode, press Space twice to begin flying so the elevated portion of the setup can be placed safely.
steps.exact_input: Space twice, if flight is needed
steps.success_cue: There is sufficient clear space for a lower rail and an upper powered rail separated vertically by an air gap.

steps.action: Select a solid block and place one block to serve as the permanent lower support. Select the normal Rail and place it on the top face of that block. This is the nearby rail onto which the falling minecart will land.
steps.exact_input: Right-click/place one solid block; then right-click/place one Rail on its top face
steps.success_cue: A single normal rail is visible on top of a solid support block.

steps.action: Build a temporary vertical pillar immediately beside the lower rail. Extend the pillar until a block can be attached directly above the lower rail while leaving exactly one full air-block space between the lower rail and that attached block.
steps.exact_input: Place temporary solid blocks beside the lower rail
steps.success_cue: The temporary pillar reaches one block beside the intended upper support position.

steps.action: Attach one solid block to the side of the temporary pillar so that it is vertically aligned with the lower rail and exactly one full air block separates this solid block from the lower rail below. This attached block is the removable block referred to as being underneath the minecart.
steps.exact_input: Right-click/place one solid block directly above the lower rail with one full air block left between them
steps.success_cue: From bottom to top, the aligned column consists of the lower support block, the normal rail, one air block, and the removable solid block.

steps.action: Select the Powered Rail and place it on top of the removable solid block. Ensure its visible track direction is parallel to the lower normal rail. Do not add a redstone power source; the supplied text specifies the powered-rail block type but does not state that it must receive power.
steps.exact_input: Right-click/place one Powered Rail on the removable solid block
steps.success_cue: The powered rail is directly above the lower normal rail, with the removable solid block and one air block between the two rails.

steps.action: Remove every block in the temporary side pillar without breaking the lower rail's permanent support, the lower rail, the vertically aligned removable support block, or the powered rail.
steps.exact_input: Left-click each temporary pillar block in Creative mode
steps.success_cue: The temporary pillar is gone, the vertical fall path is unobstructed, and both rails remain in place.

steps.action: Select the Minecart in the hotbar. Aim at the upper powered rail and use the item, normally by right-clicking, to place the minecart on that rail.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the upper Powered Rail while holding the Minecart
steps.success_cue: One minecart is resting on the upper powered rail.

steps.action: Stand at one end of the upper rail, align yourself with the direction in which the rail runs, and walk gently into the minecart to push it a small distance. Release movement immediately after the minecart shifts away from the center of the rail block. Do not push it far enough to leave the powered rail or the area above the removable support block.
steps.exact_input: Briefly press the forward movement action, default W, while contacting the minecart
steps.success_cue: The minecart remains over the removable support block but is visibly offset along the rail rather than centered on the block.

steps.action: Stop touching the minecart and wait until it is no longer rolling. If it leaves the powered rail or falls from the setup, replace it and repeat the previous step with a shorter push.
steps.success_cue: The minecart is stationary, visibly off-center, and still supported by the upper powered rail and removable block.

steps.action: Move to the side of the upper assembly so the exposed edge of the powered rail can be targeted without striking the minecart. In Creative mode, left-click the powered rail once to break only the rail underneath the minecart.
steps.success_cue: The powered rail has disappeared, while the minecart remains above and supported by the removable solid block at approximately its displaced horizontal position.

steps.action: Confirm that the lower normal rail is still directly below the minecart's fall path and that no temporary blocks obstruct the space between the minecart and that rail. Do not push or enter the minecart after removing the powered rail.
steps.success_cue: The stationary minecart is on the removable solid block, and the lower normal rail is visible below through the unobstructed fall path.

steps.action: From the side, aim at an exposed side face of the removable solid block directly underneath the minecart. Left-click that block once in Creative mode to break it without attacking the minecart. This is the trigger action; hand control to the observation subsystem as soon as the block disappears.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the removable solid block underneath the minecart
steps.success_cue: The removable support block has disappeared and the minecart is unsupported and beginning to fall toward the lower normal rail.

stor.handoff_condition: The powered rail and then the solid support block beneath the displaced minecart have been broken in that order. The minecart has just become unsupported and is beginning to fall toward the vertically aligned lower normal rail; begin observing its horizontal position and movement during contact with that rail.
uncertainties: The supplied report omits the contents of Setup.png and the other image attachments. Consequently, the exact distances, number of blocks, viewing angle, rail orientation, and any additional blocks shown in the reporter's original setup could not be preserved.

The minimum reconstructed setup uses a normal rail directly below the upper powered rail, with one air block and one removable solid support block between them. This geometry is a practical inference from the title and written sequence, not an exact transcription of the unavailable setup image.

The report does not state whether the powered rail was receiving redstone power. This plan leaves it unpowered because the report only requires the powered-rail block to be present and instructs the player to push the minecart manually.
The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected only to make item acquisition and the required two-stage block removal deterministic.

No seed, absolute coordinates, biome, dimension, world type, multiplayer environment, minecartMaxSpeed value, resource pack, or graphics setting is supplied by the report; none is added as a reproduction requirement.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-275883:Riding a minecart cluster into a wall freezes the game
source_meta._title: Minecarts become invisible if a lot of them are in the same area

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 24w34a, using the attached world.zip as a local single-player world. Preserve the world's existing experimental settings and redstone construction; do not recreate the setup in a new world or open the test copy in 24w37a.
preconditions: The attachment named world.zip is available and has not been modified.
Minecraft Launcher can launch the exact historical snapshot 24w34a; do not use the launcher entry named Latest Snapshot unless it explicitly resolves to 24w34a.
Use a separate 24w34a game directory, or at minimum retain an untouched backup of world.zip, so the test can be reset after the world's redstone state changes.
The extracted save folder containing level.dat must be installed directly under the selected installation's saves directory.
Use the controls bound to Attack/Destroy and Use Item/Place Block as applicable; the default Use Item/Place Block input is right-click.
Do not change the imported world's game mode, experimental feature configuration, command blocks, redstone components, or minecart arrangement before following the reset step.

steps.action: Make an untouched backup copy of the attached world.zip. Perform the reproduction on a separate working copy so the original saved redstone and entity state remains reusable.
steps.success_cue: An unchanged original archive and a separate working copy of world.zip are available.

steps.action: Open Minecraft Launcher, select Minecraft: Java Edition, and open the Installations tab. Enable snapshot versions in the version filter if necessary, create a new installation, and select the exact version 24w34a. Assign a separate game directory to this installation if possible. Do not select 24w37a, because that is listed as a fix version. Official snapshot instructions confirm that snapshots are enabled from the Installations tab. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-snapshot-24w34a?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A launcher installation explicitly displaying version 24w34a is selected and ready to start.

steps.action: Use the folder icon for the 24w34a launcher installation to open its game directory. Open its saves folder, creating that folder if it is absent. Extract the working copy of world.zip. If extraction creates nested wrapper folders, move the innermost folder that directly contains level.dat into saves; level.dat must not remain buried an extra folder level below the world folder. Java Edition downloaded worlds are installed by extracting the folder containing level.dat into the saves directory. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AMap_downloads?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The saves directory contains one extracted world folder, and level.dat is directly inside that world folder.

steps.action: Return to Minecraft Launcher and start the installation that explicitly identifies itself as snapshot 24w34a. Wait for the Java Edition main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft: Java Edition main menu is open under version 24w34a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer. In the world list, select the newly imported world corresponding to the extracted attachment and choose Play Selected World. Do not choose Create New World. If an experimental-world warning appears, acknowledge it and continue without changing the world's experiments or recreating the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> <imported attached world> -> Play Selected World
steps.success_cue: The player enters the attached world's prebuilt test area rather than a newly generated world.

steps.action: Do not operate any controls in the build yet. Wait until the loading screen has disappeared, surrounding chunks and the redstone construction are rendered, and camera movement and player movement respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The prebuilt world is fully rendered and responsive, with no terrain-loading screen present.

steps.action: In the prebuilt test area, locate the impulse command block used as the reset control. An impulse command block is the orange/tan patterned command-block variant. Identify the button physically mounted on, or immediately associated with, that command block. Also identify the nearby piston and the separate lever next to that piston, but do not touch the lever yet. Do not open or edit the command block.
steps.success_cue: The reset button on the impulse command block and the test lever next to the piston have both been identified without either control being activated.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair directly at the button on the impulse command block and activate it exactly once with Use Item/Place Block, default right-click. This is the report's reset action for killing all minecarts currently present before starting the test.
steps.exact_input: Use Item/Place Block once (default: right-click) on the impulse-command-block button
steps.success_cue: The button visibly depresses or otherwise activates once and then returns to its unpressed position.

steps.action: Allow at least one game tick for the command block action to complete. Do not press the reset button repeatedly. If minecarts were visible in the apparatus before the press, wait until those pre-existing minecarts are gone before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: The reset button is no longer depressed, and no pre-existing visible minecarts remain in the apparatus.

steps.action: Move only as much as necessary to reach the piston control. Aim the crosshair at the lever specifically identified as being next to the piston. Preserve the lever's loaded position; do not try to force it into a presumed starting state before the test.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair is aimed at the lever next to the piston, and the lever has not yet been toggled since the reset button was pressed.

steps.action: Activate the lever exactly once with Use Item/Place Block, default right-click. Do not double-click, immediately toggle it back, or press the minecart-kill button afterward.
steps.exact_input: Use Item/Place Block once (default: right-click) on the lever next to the piston
steps.success_cue: The lever handle changes to its opposite position exactly once while the world remains loaded.

steps.action: Immediately turn the camera toward the prebuilt track or operating area where the minecarts are being produced or clustered. Release the interaction control and avoid leaving the area, pausing for an extended period, reloading the world, or changing the lever while observation proceeds.
steps.success_cue: The minecart operating or accumulation area is in view, the lever remains in its newly toggled position, and the relevant chunks remain loaded.

stor.handoff_condition: The reset button has been pressed once, the lever next to the piston has then been toggled exactly once, and the prebuilt minecart operating area is loaded and in view. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately and keep the world open without resetting, reloading, leaving the area, or toggling the lever again; the report describes a delayed occurrence, and a confirmation comment places it at approximately 30 seconds after activation.
uncertainties: The attachment contents were not available for direct inspection, so the imported world's display name, spawn orientation, exact control-station layout, and exact location of the minecart accumulation area are not known from the supplied text.
The internal folder nesting of world.zip is unknown. The executable world folder is the folder that directly contains level.dat.
The formal reproduction steps say only that the behavior occurs 'after some time'; approximately 30 seconds comes from a confirming report comment and is not a guaranteed exact timeout.

The report does not state the lever's required initial on/off position. The plan therefore preserves the position stored in the attached world and toggles it exactly once, matching the wording 'Flick the lever.'

No particular game mode, camera perspective, graphics option, render distance, simulation distance, resource pack, or player coordinates are specified. These must not be invented as mandatory conditions.

If multiple impulse command blocks, pistons, buttons, or levers exist in the attached build, the supplied text does not provide coordinates or command contents that uniquely distinguish them; use the impulse-command-block button and the lever physically next to the piston in the apparent prebuilt test station.

source_meta._title: TNT minecart does not remember ignition source when exploding from a fall

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 25w03a in a disposable vanilla world. Use single-player with cheats enabled, or a dedicated server where the reproducing player has operator permission. Perform construction and the timed priming sequence in Creative mode, then change to Survival mode immediately before releasing the frozen simulation. The report's attached screenshot, 2025-01-15_17.30.21.png, is authoritative for the timing-sensitive rail, TNT, and drop geometry.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected snapshot 25w03a; do not use fix version 25w32a or a later release.
Use a newly created or otherwise disposable world because both the TNT block and TNT minecart will damage the setup and surrounding terrain.
Enable commands by creating the world with cheats enabled, opening an existing single-player world to LAN with cheats enabled, or granting the player operator permission on a server.

Have access to the attachment 2025-01-15_17.30.21.png if possible. Its exact block spacing and orientation were not included in the supplied text, but the sequence relies on that geometry to position the TNT minecart correctly after 52 and then 28 stepped ticks.

The setup must include the TNT block, a TNT minecart, the powered-rail route shown in the attachment, a lever that powers those rails, a track exit or drop that causes the primed minecart to fall, and an accessible position close to the minecart's landing or collision point.

Before beginning the timed sequence, the lever must be off, the powered rails must be unpowered, the TNT minecart must be stationary and unprimed in its starting position, and the separate TNT block must be intact.

The player must have a flint and steel available and must wear no armor, hold no shield in either hand, possess no active Resistance effect, and have no Totem of Undying in either hand when changing to Survival mode.
If repeating the test, rebuild the complete setup and use a fresh, unprimed TNT minecart and TNT block; do not reuse the explosion-damaged remains of a previous attempt.

steps.action: Start Minecraft: Java Edition using an installation configured for snapshot 25w03a, then enter a disposable world with commands enabled.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded 25w03a world, terrain is visible, movement responds normally, and commands are permitted.

steps.action: Enter Creative mode. Press T to open chat, type the command exactly as supplied below including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The game confirms Creative mode, and the player can fly and access the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with E. Obtain at least one flint and steel, one TNT block, one minecart with TNT, the powered rails and lever required by the attachment, and any ordinary rails and solid construction blocks visible in the attachment. Move the flint and steel to a hotbar slot, meaning one of the nine slots along the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: The construction items are available, and a flint and steel is visible in the hotbar.

steps.action: Reconstruct the complete setup depicted in 2025-01-15_17.30.21.png without changing its rail length, elevations, gaps, TNT placement, lever connection, or orientation. In particular, reproduce the lever-controlled powered-rail path, the TNT minecart's starting position, the separate TNT block, and the open drop or collision route used by the minecart.
steps.success_cue: The physical setup matches the attachment, including the relative positions of the TNT block, TNT minecart, powered rails, lever, track exit, and landing area.

steps.action: Leave the lever in its off position. Confirm visually that the powered rails are dark rather than glowing red, that the TNT minecart is stationary and not flashing, and that the separate TNT block has not been ignited.
steps.success_cue: The lever is off, the powered rails are unpowered, the TNT minecart is stationary and unprimed, and the TNT block is intact.

steps.action: Confirm that the route from the TNT minecart's starting location to the drop is unobstructed and that the surrounding chunks are fully rendered. Do not begin the timed sequence while terrain is still loading.
steps.success_cue: The entire rail route and landing area are visible, and movement and commands respond normally.

steps.action: Move close enough to the separate TNT block to ignite it with the flint and steel, while remaining able to reach the lever during the frozen simulation. Remain in Creative mode.
steps.success_cue: The player can point at the TNT block and can subsequently reach the lever without rebuilding or changing the setup.

steps.action: Freeze normal world ticking. Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that ticking is frozen; entities and scheduled world changes no longer advance continuously, while the player can still move and interact.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the flint and steel using its number key or the mouse wheel. Point the crosshair at the separate TNT block and use the item with right-click once to prime that block.
steps.success_cue: The TNT block has changed into a primed TNT entity, but its fuse is not continuously advancing because normal ticking remains frozen.

steps.action: Advance the frozen simulation by exactly 52 ticks. Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter once. Do not issue the command a second time.
steps.success_cue: Exactly 52 ticks have been processed, the initial primed TNT still exists, and the simulation has returned to its frozen state.

steps.action: Move to the lever without changing any blocks or interacting with either explosive. Use right-click once on the lever to switch it on and power the powered rails.
steps.success_cue: The lever is visibly on and the connected powered rails glow red, while the world remains frozen between tick-step commands.

steps.action: Advance the frozen simulation by exactly 28 additional ticks. Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter once. Do not repeat it.
steps.success_cue: The initial TNT block has completed its fuse and detonated, the TNT minecart has been primed by that detonation, and the simulation is frozen again with the primed minecart at or entering the fall portion of the attachment's setup.

steps.action: Do not run another tick-step command. Visually identify the primed TNT minecart and determine its fall or landing point from its current position and trajectory. Do not strike, ignite, replace, or otherwise interact with the minecart.
steps.success_cue: The primed TNT minecart is present, world ticking remains frozen, and the player has identified where to stand near its imminent fall or collision.

steps.action: While still in Creative mode, remove all equipped armor through the inventory and ensure neither hand contains a shield or Totem of Undying. Clear any active Resistance effect if one was previously applied.
steps.success_cue: All four armor slots are empty, neither hand contains a protective item, and no Resistance effect is active.

steps.action: Move to the stable standing position shown or implied by the attachment near the falling TNT minecart's landing or collision point. Position the player close enough that the minecart's explosion can kill an unarmored Survival-mode player in one hit, but do not stand where merely changing game mode causes an immediate fall into the void or another unrelated hazard.
steps.success_cue: The player is on stable footing immediately beside the minecart's imminent impact area, with the primed minecart still suspended by the frozen simulation.

steps.action: Change to Survival mode while ticking is still frozen. Press T, type the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The game confirms Survival mode; hearts and hunger are visible, the player is still positioned by the impact area, and the minecart has not resumed moving.

steps.action: Without moving away, verify that normal ticking is still frozen, the player remains unarmored in Survival mode, and the primed TNT minecart is still positioned to complete its fall or collision as soon as ticking resumes.
steps.success_cue: All final trigger conditions are simultaneously established: Survival mode, lethal-range positioning, no protective equipment, a primed falling TNT minecart, and frozen world ticking.

steps.action: Release the frozen simulation. Press T, enter the following command including the leading slash, and press Enter once. Immediately hand control to the observation subsystem; do not move, pause, or enter another command.
steps.success_cue: Normal world ticking has resumed and the previously paused primed TNT minecart is free to continue its fall or collision.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just executed /tick unfreeze while standing unarmored in Survival mode at lethal range of the primed TNT minecart's imminent fall or collision. Normal ticking has resumed and the cart has been released to complete that movement; begin observation immediately.
uncertainties: The supplied report text refers to attachment 2025-01-15_17.30.21.png but does not include the image itself. Consequently, the exact number of powered rails, rail orientation, elevations, horizontal distances, TNT placement, drop height, and player standing location cannot be recovered from the supplied evidence without inventing geometry.

Web verification was attempted using the permitted Minecraft and Mojira domains, but the issue attachment's contents and attachment identifier were not available. The plan therefore preserves the attachment as the authoritative setup rather than substituting an unverified rail design.

The report does not explicitly state single-player versus dedicated server. A cheats-enabled single-player world is selected as the simplest execution environment because no multiplayer-only condition is described.

The exact lethal standing distance is not numerically specified. The executor must preserve the screenshot's positioning or choose a stable position immediately adjacent to the minecart's impact area while unarmored.

The report notes inherent random fuse timing for a TNT minecart. A run can exceptionally detonate before ground contact; rebuild the setup and repeat the same sequence if the minecart detonates before completing the intended fall or collision, but do not repeatedly trigger explosions within one setup.
